QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_56

question.text: Are there any restrictions on speculative trading in ETIRD markets?

answer.text: Speculators can trade in ETIRD, but positions are subject to applicable SEBI / exchange limits by participant category and other regulatory restrictions
Speculative trading is completely banned in ETIRD
Speculators have higher position limits than other participant categories
There are no restrictions on speculative trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (pp.90, 159, 234-237, 286), speculation in financial derivatives is permitted and speculators are vital to ETIRD market liquidity, but every participant — including speculators — is subject to SEBI / exchange position limits by participant category and other regulatory restrictions. The Trap: Speculation is not banned. The "no restrictions" option contradicts position-limit tables. The "higher than other categories" option is not stated in the workbook. Note: Anchor the answer to "position limits by participant category"; the workbook does not state a general rule that speculator limits are lower than hedger limits.
